summary.text: A 34-week premature infant born by cesarean section as the smaller of twins, with a birth weight of 2,550 grams and Apgar scores of 10 at 1 and 5 minutes, developed moaning and tachypnea shortly after birth and was admitted to the neonatal unit. After feeding began the infant had recurrent non-bilious vomiting and gastric retention, and progressive abdominal distension despite fasting and gastric decompression.

An x-ray at the referring hospital showed pneumoperitoneum and the infant was transferred. On admission the infant was stable with a distended, rigid abdomen with absent bowel sounds and normal laboratory tests. A repeat x-ray showed free subdiaphragmatic air and the football sign, confirming spontaneous neonatal gastric perforation.

Given stable hemodynamics the team performed emergent laparoscopic repair under combined intravenous-inhalational anesthesia. Findings were a large muscular layer defect along the greater curvature with serosal tearing and two approximately 2 mm perforations with purulent exudate. Devitalized tissue was resected, the defect closed and reinforced, and a drain placed; the procedure took 47 minutes with 20 mL blood loss.

Postoperative NICU care included broad-spectrum antibiotics, decompression and parenteral nutrition. A contrast study on postoperative day 7 showed complete healing and the tubes were removed. Standard formula caused rash and reflux that resolved on amino acid-based formula. Full enteral feeding was achieved by day 17, discharge followed on day 20, pathology showed a congenital gastric musculature defect, and one-month follow-up was satisfactory.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 2
Sequential intraoperative views of the laparoscopic repair for spontaneous neonatal gastric perforation. (A) Intraoperative inspection identified extensive serosal tearing and muscularis defects, featuring two perforations (approximately 2 mm, arrows) surrounded by purulent exudate. (B) Isolation and clamping of the short gastric vessels using Hemlock forceps, with careful preservation of the posterior gastric vessels. (C) Resection of the non-viable gastric tissue and the muscularis defect using laparoscopic scissors. (D) Continuous suture closure of the gastric defect along the greater curvature with 4-0 barbed suture. Reinforcement of the suture line with interrupted 5-0 VICRYL sutures. (E) Final appearance of the repaired stomach following suture reinforcement. (F) Postoperative schematic of trocar placements: 1, secondary working port; 2, primary working port; 3, camera port; 4, assistant port; 5, liver retractor port.
